title: STA-24: cases the disposition decisions leave open
description:
The amendment of 2026-10-13 (ADR-0044) wrote the disposition rule into `STA-24` and `STA-20b` in the decisions' own words. These cases are not answered by those words. Each is recorded here so that it is decided by its owner and not by an implementation; none is a rule until decided.

1. **A harness job the model requests by name.** `STA-24` refuses "the model's box-plane commands to that machine" under a destructive continuation. `ARC-43` says `fetch_artifact` and `ready_to_reset` "run under the box-plane scope like any `exec`", and `place_secret` is box-plane work too. Whether a job the model requests through `request_harness_job` is one of the model's commands is not said. The companion's `exec` stands for box-plane work as a whole.
2. **A further disposition that names only the unresolved rescue activation.** `STA-24`: "One disposition stands per resource, the latest". If the rescue activation of a standing reinstall goes unresolved and the operator disposes of it alone with a continuing choice, that disposition replaces the reinstall one, and the box-plane stop the disposed reset carried is gone. This follows from the words; whether it is wanted is the owner's to confirm.
3. **A call disposed by a disposition since replaced** can never be named again: `STA-24` lets a replacement name only "the calls the standing one disposed".
4. **Where `STG-20`'s installation boundary falls** relative to the disposition and the reset into rescue, and so when the installed pin retires. `STA-24` keeps the pinned SSH attempt permitted while a destructive disposition stands, which needs a pin.
5. **A continuing choice with a pin already recorded.** `STA-20b` makes keeping the current rescue boot and running the install again "continuing as if not done"; `CHN-R7` lets no installed-system pin replace an active one without a reinstall. An install that regenerates host keys then cannot be pinned.
6. **The rescue activation that counts.** The companion reads `STA-24`'s "after that rescue activation is confirmed" as an activation dispatched after the standing disposition was recorded, confirmed, with no reset after it. An activation confirmed before the disposition with no reset since, and one dispatched under a disposition since replaced, do not count, and a new activation is admitted. Narrow by intent; confirm or widen.
7. **Untyped scopes.** A destructive disposition on a scope that is not a vendor's; the hold across a re-approved scope, a rotated token or a grown bound set; and how a reinstall or an abandonment is carried out by hand (already `TASKS.md` T47).
8. **`docs/briefs/01-install.md`** tells a model in rescue to read the Resume section before wiping and to preserve existing host keys. After a reinstall's fresh rescue boot that steers it to continue the install the operator chose to discard.
close_reason: Settled decisions implemented in requirements, formal companion, witness files, controls and conformance records

comments.text: Open case from review of the pull request (2026-10-14): a rescue activation spent by a reboot the harness did not request. STA-24 counts a rescue activation dispatched after the standing disposition, confirmed, with no reset intent after it; TauWeb.Dispatch.rescueConfirmed ignores observations. Trace: reinstall disposition, activation confirmed, an unexpected reboot observed (the activation is used by that boot), then a reset: it counts as the reset into rescue and ends the restriction, though with the activation spent it boots the installed system. Contact with that system is still stopped by the pin (the rescue pin does not match), so no command lands; the gap is that the reset is treated as the continuation. To decide: whether an observed reboot (a reset predicate reporting ended or succeeded, not any read of it) spends the activation, in STA-24's sentence and in rescueConfirmed. Dedicated path only; LNVPS has one reinstall call.

comments.author: user
comments.text:
Decided: the spent-activation case. STA-24 now says "the reset into rescue is a reset dispatched after that rescue activation is confirmed and while the newest read of that activation still confirms it". TauWeb.Dispatch.spent_activation_not_counted carries the refusal after a non-confirming newest activation read, the activation call remaining terminal, and the later admitted reset after a fresh activation confirmed. STG-4 owns the immediate re-read and durable journal duty for this disposition's reset.

New open case: the ordinary install ceremony's own reset into rescue, with no disposition, has the same window. A reboot nobody requested spends the activation, and the reset then boots the installed system. Nothing refuses that reset before dispatch. Its harm is bounded by the pin check: if /rescue/last still holds the pre-reset snapshot's keys, the reset-into-rescue predicate never holds, its barrier stands, and the operator disposes. If the unrequested boot publishes fresh disjoint keys after that snapshot but before the harness's reset lands, those keys can satisfy the predicate; the pinned SSH attempt remains the bound. This window is not closed. The ordinary ceremony and its conformance cases are unchanged; this issue stays open with its other undecided cases.

title: State-machine clarity and composition atlas
description:
## Outcome
A navigable behavioral atlas of the existing specification, plus a separately scoped session-authority assurance track. This is a work plan, not a specification amendment. Checkpoint 0 is recorded below; no atlas implementation was made while filing it.

## Source and baseline
The owner's State-Machine Clarity and Composition Plan, prepared 2026-11-01, checkpoints 0–5 and Recommended first change, is transferred into this epic and its child descriptions so execution does not require a temporary plan file.

Working revision: 9086166b0ee62387da6440da059f5b89f01a0d8d on main, initially clean. It equals the reviewed baseline exactly; there are no intervening committed amendments to reconcile. The actual tree, owners and current witness files were inspected rather than treating the plan's review as current authority.

Baseline command, run unpiped on 2026-11-01: `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh`. Actual result: exit 0, “All gates passed.” Formal, witnesses, regions, identifiers, fixtures, obligations, citations and coverage all passed. No pre-existing failing gate or missing toolchain. This command does not run the mutation controls; no current controls pass is claimed. Subsequent implementation must run the required gates before and after, and controls for any changed refusal checks.

## Bounded first delivery
Use the Stage applicability and admission table in 07-conformance.md as the source list: stage-1 typed LNVPS, local authority, interruption, delivery, re-entry and maintained-cloud Restore/Replace. Distinguish typed restart confirmation from guest boot, service survival and delivery checking. Dedicated delivery_reboot/rescue, attest, untyped calls, multi-machine tenants and paid relay retain their own applicability. A synthetic witness or documentation pass admits no production capability, procured-inference minting, vendor behavior or browser/device conformance.

## Existing diagram inventory
Locations are at the working revision. Preserve useful figures and route readers to them; do not claim that the repository lacks state diagrams.

| Existing view | Location | Treatment / class |
|---|---|---|
| System context | 00-overview.md, System context (Mermaid near line 143) | Navigation: keep; label conceptual and show stage-1 route separately from attest and larger sets. |
| Two planes | 01-architecture.md, Two planes (near line 126) | Navigation: keep; index approval and binding owners, including inference's separate route. |
| Concurrent sessions | 01-architecture.md, concurrency (near line 645) | Navigation: keep; default singleton illustration, keys remain machine-owned, not new session-owned keys. |
| Recovery ladder state diagram | 01-architecture.md, ARC-16 (near line 742) | Presentation: qualify Retry with STA-5/STA-6/STA-8/STA-24 pointers; third-rung behavior remains the semantic question tw-ae7. |
| Routes to a fingerprint | 02-channel.md (near line 32) | Navigation: keep route/admission and pending evidence distinctions; the admitted LNVPS route is not completed integrated conformance. |
| Attest sequence | 02-channel.md, CHN-4 (near line 360) | Navigation plus missing evidence: retain route-specific label; do not promote it to the stage-1 path or a full durability/first-contact proof. |
| Trust tiers | 05-trust.md (near line 10) | Navigation: keep; outside the behavioral transition core. |
| Dedicated installation sequence | 06-first-stage.md, The sequence (near line 273) | Navigation: keep as construction-test-bed sequence, not stage-1 LNVPS evidence. |
| Recovery by access/vendor | 03-state-and-recovery.md (near line 907) | Presentation: keep and qualify “Zero downtime” as key/pin recovery rather than live session/scan/allocation authority; preserve the existing ARC-22 LNVPS pointer. “Always works” is a design route, not integrated device evidence. |

The archived rust-first-ai-harness-pwa-spec.md has an ASCII component diagram near line 151; retain it as archive, not current authority. Mermaid inventory was searched across repository Markdown. No replacement diagram is needed for every existing figure.

## High-level word audit and classification
The classes below are those of plan checkpoint 0; each proposed change has one primary class. Navigation and presentation changes preserve behavior. Missing evidence remains a named boundary; semantic decisions remain outside the clarity track.

| Word / finding | Owner and observed distinction | Class / destination |
|---|---|---|
| retry | ARC-16 and CONTEXT.md's Recovery ladder compress recovery to “Retry”; STA-5's vendor retry classes and STA-6's box-plane rule are elsewhere. STA-8: “It MUST NOT be retried automatically and no timer may clear it.” | Presentation: route the ladder to these owners; never draw automatic replay of an uncertain effect. |
| resume | ARC-22's Resume-or-abandon opening screen, STG-12, ARC-10's read/converge, STA-7's replay, STA-20's stopped wait and STA-23's processed suspension/end are distinct. STA-7: “**No model turn is silently resumed from an uncertain destructive operation.**” | Navigation: index each continuation boundary. Missing evidence for real device scheduling belongs to existing conformance, not a new arrow. |
| ready | ready_to_reset belongs to ARC-43/STA-20b and current-installation prerequisite evidence. STG-21a: “It does not establish a completed guest boot or service survival.” Running-state readiness, pin eligibility, scan readiness, allocation permission and admission are distinct. 07-conformance.md separates construction from delivery admission. | Navigation: preserve independent predicates; no global Ready enum or universal gate. |
| delivered | ARC-17, ARC-39 and ARC-43 own verdict, findings, declaration and local evidence labels; executive-summary.md already distinguishes findings and report authority. ARC-17: “placement itself clears no finding.” | Navigation: keep the current delivery distinctions, including lifecycle findings permitting placement and the post-placement demonstration. |
| confirmed | STG-21a owns operation-specific LNVPS predicates; STG-4 owns Robot's different predicates; STA-3/STA-24 own durable acceptance. Restart receipt, guest boot, service survival, accepted pin and final verdict are different. | Navigation: map observation to exact authority; do not apply Robot status-read confirmation to LNVPS restart or imply billing ends at stop. |
| Recovery chart's Zero downtime / Always works | STA-17/STA-22b restore known identities with no new allocation authority; STA-23 ends lost runtime authority; ARC-17/SEC-5/ARC-43 retain findings/scan re-check duties. | Presentation: qualify at the figure's owner without inventing the missing restored-command rule (tw-ub7). |
| Session/dispatch composition | Dispatch.lean's opening docstring assumes termination and single-writer convention; pending-check/lifecycle reads, untyped pause/hold, detailed protected encodings/listing selection and inference clocks are omitted. | Missing evidence: explicit prose-only labels; selected assurance child handles only session-authority seam. |
| Relay coverage | Relay.lean's header explicitly retains a historical profile; current /v2/ behavior is outside it. TASKS.md open T30 is the existing port owner. | Missing evidence: point to that owner; no duplicate current-relay task. |
| Delivery reboot trace task drift | tw-itv's no-trace claim is stale: schema-8 file and Dispatch.lean contain command_holds_delivery_reboot / delivery_reboot_without_hold; check-controls.sh has the drop-reboot control. rebootRequest still copies execRequest facts and uses approvalExec. | Missing evidence: retain tw-itv for distinct approval and bounded-description remainder; do not duplicate or claim closed. |
| Witness pair integrity | check_witnesses.py checks emission drift; tw-316 owns reciprocal pair/start/events/changed-assumptions validation. | Missing evidence: link existing bead; local atlas selected-pair checks must not create a competing corpus-wide gate. |

## Semantic decisions already owned elsewhere
These do not block filing or the first atlas change. Label the affected cells “not specified” and link the existing question. Do not settle them in a renderer or completion claim.

| Existing owner | Distinguishing history / conflicting boundary |
|---|---|
| tw-ae7 | ARC-16: “then destroy the machine and restart under a different domain, which costs a server.” ARC-22 offers different LNVPS stop/renewal-off and reinstall stand-ins. A stuck stage-1 machine reaches rung three: same-machine reinstall versus stopped old machine plus new order versus no third rung remains undecided. |
| tw-ub7 | STA-24: “What this rule cannot reach is a journal that is lost with the phone”. STA-20's hold is journal-derived, but on-machine persistent records survive. Restore an older backup after a command send; then request another command: whether to collect old records before sends is unsettled. |
| tw-pgp | STA-24's untyped-vendor destructive hold names “the model's box-plane commands”; ADR-0050's machine destructive rule stops work whoever starts it. Dispose an untyped vendor call destructively, then request a harness-composed job: no silent extension from typed behavior. Stage 2 boundary. |
| tw-pkn | SEC-5 row 23 retires a reference at machine destruction; CNF-95(f) retains A/B withholding until both references are rebuilt, and ADR-0050 rejects output release without scanning copied secrets. Destroy M while A still withholds output possibly containing M's secret: release/continued-scan outcome remains undecided. Stage 2 boundary. |
| tw-z99 | STA-24: “An unresolved activation or key registration touches no running system and blocks nothing on the box.” ADR-0048 admits delivery reboot beside activation. Activate rescue, then delivery reboot: a changed boot can be rescue rather than the installed delivery target. Dedicated-route decision. |
| tw-sfu, tw-hwl, tw-nj8 | Definitive create failure while a session still owns its set: failure evidence and later sends, successor allocation on the same entry, and ordering a different entry are separate undecided boundaries. Do not promote unresolved/disposed/stop to failure or drop old membership. |
| tw-yuo | The phase-B finding establishes a pinned arch login, while STA-20 needs a root-only job directory and delivery reads need privileged access. Login then create a root-only job record: no owner yet defines the privilege route, authorization or refusal. Keep this existing stage-1 question explicit; do not guess a sudo policy. |
| tw-lq8 | Rescue rekeys a dedicated machine under a fresh seed after sheet loss; the shown installation identity changes while its root label can remain stale. The next rescue install can misread its own root as a predecessor. Installation ordinal, relabel ordering and migration remain this later-route owner's question. |
| tw-l1l, tw-yhd | Reinstall target/acceptance history and recovery outside a session retain their existing questions. Sheetless discovery/listing alone must not become cloud-destroy authorization. |

The existing proposed operator-reported key-revocation amendment remains tw-i55, not a new atlas task. No newly discovered behavior decision blocks this transfer. The session-authority child must stop at an actual new ambiguity and capture clauses plus distinguishing history before seeking a decision. OPN-27 remains the tenant architecture owner; empirical recovery/scanning retain OPN-3/OPN-18/OPN-28 and their conformance applicability.

## Constraints inherited by every child
One normative home per rule and argument; checked quotes and pointers elsewhere. Formal authority remains per clause under ADR-0032; outside covered formal regions Markdown stays authoritative. Use formal companion terminology. No new runtime framework, state-machine engine, theorem registry or copied guard implementation. No theorem, gate, assumption or requirement weakened to make a picture agree. No runtime code in this repository. Keep conformance identifiers out of Lean, witness files and marked-region emissions. Do not reuse authority-bearing formal markers for informational projections without a separate semantics review. No behavior change inside a documentation change.

## Coverage and ordering
The first implementation child owns the Recommended first change: atlas skeleton, combined authority/barrier/command-hold matrix and generated Dispatch pairs with the minimal faithful rendering/checking slice. Subsequent children own expanded composition/owner presentation, remaining trace curation/renderer coverage, independent session-authority assurance, and clarity review/handoff. This is seam-based filing, not a ticket per plan subsection.

Plan coverage: §§2,4 and boundaries are here and inherited; §5 and Recommended first change start in the first child; §6 and owner presentation finish in composition; §7 scenarios and renderer/controls finish in trace expansion; §8 is separate assurance; §§9–10 clarity close in review/handoff. Assurance is not a blocker for clarity. Existing semantic questions, witness-pair validation, delivery-reboot remainder and relay port retain their original owners.

## Success Criteria
Before implementation, re-read owners at the then-current revision and rerun the unpiped Nix gate. Track actual commands/results and distinguish fixtures from implementation evidence. Final clarity acceptance requires a reader locating each owner, source-attributed per-step views, deterministic regeneration/controls, visible bounds and missing evidence, plus an exact downstream comparison and device/adapter fault-evidence contract. Targeted assurance additionally needs reviewed property statements, successful paths, discriminating negative controls and an authority/Dispatch seam test. This filing is not a launch-readiness panel or an implementation pass.

## Filed seams
- tw-237.1 — Recommended first change; no implementation blocker; related tw-316 and tw-itv.
- tw-237.2 — Composition reference and owner presentation; blocked by tw-237.1.
- tw-237.3 — Remaining trace/renderer coverage; blocked by tw-237.1; related tw-316 and tw-itv.
- tw-237.4 — Separate authority assurance; blocked by tw-237.1; does not block clarity.
- tw-237.5 — Reader exercise and downstream handoff; blocked by tw-237.2 and tw-237.3.

Tracker filing remains uncommitted on plan/state-machine-atlas: docs/agents/issue-tracker.md requires JSONL with its tracked change but does not require a standalone planning PR. No implementation or issue closure is part of checkpoint 0.

description:

Land the plan's Recommended first change as a useful, checked vertical slice: docs/state-machine-atlas.md skeleton, entry links, a combined authority/barrier/command-hold matrix, a generated Dispatch lost-response uncertainty pair and a generated machine-command-hold pair. This is the first implementation child of tw-237.

## Why this exists
Readers need to find the owning rule and determine what remains blocked after one restriction clears. This slice tests the proposed presentation before expanding the renderer or proofs. The starting specification revision and checkpoint-0 inventory are in tw-237; reconcile with the then-current tree before editing.

## Scope
- Add the atlas entry point and link from README.md and 00-overview.md. Outline store/writer, session/approvals, cloud/reconciliation, commands, identity/pins, delivery/secrets, allocation/recovery regions. Keep only short routing links in owner chapters.
- For this slice, fill the combined authority, unresolved cloud barrier, unresolved command and standing destructive disposition matrix. Cover typed mutation, adapter reconciliation read, ordinary exec, harness-owned job, record collection, pin-checked connection, inference and actionable publication. Use allowed-subject-to-other-guards, refused, held and not-specified distinctly; preserve specified ordering without inventing universal refusal precedence. Pending-check, scan/protected-evidence and identity-exclusion expansion follows in the composition child, with pointers/boundaries visible now.
- Each view distinguishes recorded knowledge, external possibilities and permitted actions. Give every view its own conceptual-navigation/generated-witness/general-theorem/implementation-evidence label and a brief glossary. Attribute the exact property, assumptions and bound locally.
- Implement the minimal deterministic tools/render_state_machine_atlas.py and its check/tests; extend check-all.sh/check-controls.sh only as needed. Use informational markers distinct from formal authority regions. Prefer trace tables; compact Mermaid only where useful.
- Select the schema-8 Dispatch same_action_new_call_id_refused / same_action_new_call_id_admitted pair and second_command_held / second_command_without_hold pair by their actual declarations. The former witnesses uncertainty after missing terminal evidence; its source contains no explicit lost-response or replay event. Explain the driver absence without fabricating either event, a timestamp or a real external outcome. Keep both sides whole, identify the admitted side as a withdrawn-guard counterexample rather than a permissible success. Add nearby source-backed progress, including hold_reads_and_other_machines with terminal collection and subsequent dispatch; other-machine steps remain stage-1 fixtures, not admission of multi-machine sessions; preserve any pair metadata on other selected progress witnesses too. If a chosen progress source is itself paired, render its partner as well.
- Explain worker replay with its exact source property/pointer, not an inserted event in the fresh-call pair. Do not splice witnesses and call the result checked composition.

## Critical constraints and failure handling
Inherit tw-237's boundaries: one normative home, checked quotations/pointers rather than copied guard logic, per-clause authority, no behavior amendment, no new engine or runtime implementation. Quote a requirement when asserting what it says. STA-8: “It MUST NOT be retried automatically and no timer may clear it.” No local session or call identifier erases remote uncertainty.

The renderer projects committed per-step outcomes and knowledge; it never evaluates guards or authors expected outcomes. Validate exact supported schema/module/shape and declaration resolution. Reject ambiguous selection rather than taking a silent first match: the current Dispatch file has declarations reused by multiple receipt cases. Escape labels safely. Preserve event order, start, assumptions, bound and pairs; no CNF identifiers in emissions. No complete-alphabet or full-browser proof claim.

## Dependencies / ordering
No implementation blocker. This is the first change, before expanding composition/traces or session assurance. Related tw-316 remains the owner of corpus-wide marked-pair shape validation; validate selected inputs locally without duplicating that project-wide work. Related tw-itv retains its approval-facts remainder; current command/reboot hold traces already exist. Neither blocks showing the existing exec hold pair. Existing semantic questions in tw-237 become named not-specified boundaries, not guessed cells.

## Acceptance Criteria
Run `nix develop --command bash tools/check-all.sh` unpiped before and after. Demonstrate deterministic regeneration and check-mode success on valid source. Add discriminating checks/controls for stale output, unknown schema, missing selected witness, unresolved declaration, changed source step outcome with stale rendered output, malformed/unsupported shape, missing local evidence label, and unsafe label escaping. Each new refusal gate needs a mutation control requiring exactly one finding under its target label plus a positive valid-input control where blanket rejection could pass. Run the relevant controls under the repository's prescribed resource cap, record actual results and show selected source-to-rendered per-step agreement. Faithful rendering proves presentation only. No live vendor or browser conformance result is owed by this bead.

## Spec refs
Owner's plan §§2,4–5,6.2,7.1,7.3 and Recommended first change, transferred in tw-237. Owners: STA-1–STA-8, STA-20, STA-23, STA-24, SEC-1, SEC-4, ARC-43, docs/design/witness-file-v1.md, ADR-0032. Keep ARC-16's third-rung decision under tw-ae7.

title: Complete atlas composition references and correct recovery presentation
description:
## Outcome
Finish the atlas's state-region, transition and evidence reference, and extend the first change's matrix so overlapping restrictions have explicit source-backed outcomes. Correct the misleading high-level presentation identified in tw-237 at its owning figure while preserving current behavior.

## Why this exists
A cleared cloud barrier is not a delivered machine, a usable approval is not live session authority, and restored metadata is not permission for a new allocation. Readers need one navigable composition index without a second rule registry.

## Scope
For each region in the initial atlas, record owner, identity/key, authoritative source, durable/transient fields, derived predicates and authority invalidation: store/writer (STA-1–STA-3/STA-7/STA-23); session (STA-23/SEC-1/SEC-4/ARC-12/ARC-31a); cloud (STA-4/STA-8/STA-24 and vendor predicates); commands (STA-20/STA-20b/ARC-43); pins/identity (CHN-R routes/SEC-11/protected evidence); delivery (ARC-17/ARC-39/ARC-43/SEC-5); allocation/recovery (STA-17/STA-22 family and credential format).

Add transition records for dispatch, result acceptance, job-record collection, disposition, session end, processed suspension/continuation, pin retirement and delivery publication. Each record routes event/provenance, affected identity, preconditions, durable boundary, changed and unchanged regions, permitted effects, failed append/lost reply/duplicate/stale result/interruption/re-entry and exact companion coverage to their owners. Generate available fields; otherwise use checked quotes/pointers. Never reimplement guards in a table.

Complete matrix overlaps for pending post-restart delivery check, scan readiness/protected evidence, identity quarantine/store-level exclusions and any deferred untyped-vendor restrictions. Keep action classes from the first child. A read allowed by one barrier still requires all other authority, pins and output protection. Keep not-specified questions separate from refusals and held requests; no new universal first-error precedence.

Add observation-to-authority map for vendor receipts/status reads, job records, host-key publications, boot changes, notifications and model-written reports. LNVPS restart confirmation, observed guest boot, service-survival reads and final durable verdict are separate. ARC-43 pending-check hold and lifecycle reads remain prose-only unless separately extended.

Presentation corrections at owner: qualify ARC-16's Retry with STA-5/STA-6/STA-8/STA-24 pointers; qualify the recovery figure's Zero downtime / Always works with its actual key/pin recovery and empirical boundaries. Preserve the useful existing figures in tw-237. Do not choose LNVPS rung-three semantics, invent a post-Restore command hold or turn recovery into allocation/session/scan authority.

## Non-goals and failure handling
Inherit all tw-237 constraints. No behavior changes, theorem weakening, formal-region authority change, runtime implementation, capability admission or new conformance list. Keep checked quotations with assertions about requirements and link the source list instead of restating counts. Any actual conflicting rules get clauses plus a distinguishing history and a decision at the owner; unaffected atlas work continues.

## Dependencies / ordering
Blocked by the initial atlas slice. Related existing semantic owners: tw-ae7 (third rung), tw-ub7 (pre-loss command after Restore), tw-pgp (untyped destructive hold), tw-pkn (destruction/output), tw-z99 (rescue activation/reboot), tw-sfu/tw-hwl/tw-nj8 (failure/successors), tw-l1l (installation acceptance), tw-yhd (sheetless destroy). Link these at affected cells; none blocks documenting the gap. Do not create new tasks for their existing questions.

Dispatch.lean assumes an ended session sends no further request and does not prove termination. Independent local properties are insufficient to establish that stale asynchronous work cannot revive authority or bypass a journal-derived barrier.

Use processed events and symbolic authority/session/binding identities; keep durable historical evidence separate from live runtime authority. No instantaneous physical app-switch or guaranteed cleanup observation.

Review these plan proof targets, not new requirements by fiat:
- Ended authority cannot admit a new ordinary effect or actionable publication.
- Stale approval/late completion cannot restore it or transfer across sessions/bindings.
- Ordinary visibility-only hide outside backup ceremony preserves eligible sessions.
- Processed suspension requires the specified validation before ordinary sends/publication, with no assumption every freeze was reported.
- Lock/replay/expiry leaves remote uncertainty intact and supplies no permission to repeat it.

Connect authority decisions through a small explicit interface to existing Dispatch behavior; reuse its barrier rather than copying guards. Separate authorization properties from real implementation pre-send/post-await fences and storage ordering. Already accepted remote work can continue after local authority ends. title: ARC-16's third rung at LNVPS has no form: a reinstall of the same machine, or a stop plus a new order
description:
`ARC-16` says "Recovery is a ladder." It continues: "Retry; then escalate to a stronger model behind the same proxy; then destroy the machine and restart under a different domain, which costs a server." Its diagram's note on the destroy reads "Never handed to another session." and "Costs a server." Stage 1 offers that rung: `STG-17` says "`ARC-16` says "then escalate to a stronger model behind the same proxy", and the harness **MUST NOT** use the candidate order as that rung: the first stage offers rungs one and three only, and says so."

LNVPS has no destroy route, and `ARC-22` gives destroy and recreate two different stand-ins there, which the third rung needs at once. `ARC-22` says "Where the harness would destroy a machine — an abandonment, or the old machine of a Replace rebuild — it stops that machine, turns automatic renewal off, and shows it as still existing and billed, with the vendor's stated deletion date, until deletion is confirmed under the LNVPS operation contract." It also says "**Where the harness would recreate a machine** to re-run its first contact, a vendor-API reinstall of the same machine stands in and is a **new first contact**: the old pin does not authorize contact with the reinstalled system; `CHN-R7` governs the publication route and installed-pin retirement, while a different eligible source follows its own admission rule." The specification leaves undecided whether the successor reuses that machine through reinstall or receives a new order after the old machine is stopped.

What the choice touches:

- **Exposure.** `SEC-1` says "A model that has touched a machine counts as touching it until that machine is destroyed, because ending a session does not remove whatever the model may already have left behind." At LNVPS, destruction is the vendor's confirmed deletion: `SEC-5` row 12's "How it dies" cell reads "Machine destroyed (at LNVPS, the vendor's confirmed deletion, not the stop that stands in for a destroy, `ARC-22`), or operator rotates". `SEC-1` also says "Where a profile declares an independence bound, the recovery ladder's middle rung and re-entry stay inside this rule only while the configured model's **footprint** — every machine it has touched, and every machine co-bound with those — stays within that bound for the life of those machines; past that rung the machine is destroyed rather than handed on." and "Where no bound is declared, the footprint is counted and shown (`OVR-6`), and neither the rung nor a re-entry is refused for it." Stage 1's ad-hoc profile declares none: its "Independence bound" section reads "None declared."
- **A precedent.** On the dedicated path, where the server is rented rather than created, the bottom rung is already a reinstall: `STG-20` says "So the harness's response is `ARC-16`'s bottom rung applied to this path: if the installed system does not answer on the channel within `installed.wait_max` (`bundle/timing.toml`) of the reset that should have booted it, the session declares the install failed, tells the operator, and **offers a return to rescue and reinstallation from the brief** — the same ceremony, and cheap (about five minutes when it works)."
- **A new order's price.** Each LNVPS machine has its own account: `STG-21` says "Before the first order under each machine's identity, the typed LNVPS adapter MUST submit the operator's own email address to that account at the vendor." It continues: "LNVPS sends a single-use verification link valid for about a day; the operator opens it." A new order therefore needs a new per-machine identity (ADR-0042), a new verification and a new invoice, while the stopped machine stays shown as billed until its deletion date. `STG-18` says "Stage 1 buys one LNVPS machine by one invoice through the per-machine identity decided in ADR-0042."
- **Coverage.** No conformance item exercises `ARC-16`'s third rung at any vendor.

Options:

- **A — a reinstall of the same machine** under the successor session, as `ARC-22`'s recreate form: a new installation and a new first contact; the stuck model's footprint keeps the machine, counted and shown where no bound is declared; `ARC-16`'s "Never handed to another session" gains a qualifier; where a profile declares a bound, `SEC-1` already requires the destroy form (B).
- **B — a stop plus a new order**: `ARC-22`'s destroy form for the old machine, which stays shown as existing and billed until its deletion date and in the stuck model's footprint until the vendor's confirmed deletion, and a new order under a new identity for the successor session, with its own verification and invoice.
- **C — no third rung at LNVPS in stage 1**: amend `STG-17` to offer only rung one there; the operator abandons (`ARC-22`) and starts a new setup with the goal entered again.

Decide which form the third rung takes at LNVPS; whether it differs by declared bound; and whether a conformance item exercises it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] If A or B is chosen, `ARC-16` or `ARC-22` (or both) states the third rung's form at LNVPS, and whether it differs where a profile declares an independence bound. If C is chosen, `STG-17` is amended to offer only rung one at LNVPS in stage 1. `ARC-16` says "Retry; then escalate to a stronger model behind the same proxy; then destroy the machine and restart under a different domain, which costs a server."
- [ ] `STG-17` says what stage 1 offers at LNVPS. Today it says "`ARC-16` says "then escalate to a stronger model behind the same proxy", and the harness **MUST NOT** use the candidate order as that rung: the first stage offers rungs one and three only, and says so."
- [ ] Every sentence the decision makes false is amended in the same change: `ARC-16`'s diagram notes "Never handed to another session." and "Costs a server.", and `SEC-1`'s "Where no bound is declared, the footprint is counted and shown (`OVR-6`), and neither the rung nor a re-entry is refused for it."
- [ ] If A or B is chosen, a `CNF` item exercises the third rung at LNVPS, or the stage applicability table says why none is owed. If C is chosen, the stage applicability table records why no third-rung exercise is owed at LNVPS in stage 1.
- [ ] Once on main, twr-qso in tau-web-rust can close.

title: Clarify lifecycle findings when no secret placement occurs
description:
Owner clarification needed after the decisions 15–17 amendment (tw-formal-companion-4l6), at revision 96f1b57.

ARC-17 in 01-architecture.md says "Any lifecycle failure before placement is not a finding, whether or not the declared service needs the secret to start". Its general delivery rule also says a machine is delivered only when the delivery check finds no difference from the declaration, and otherwise provides handover with findings. ARC-39 and docs/design/delivery-declaration-v1.md allow declaring services without requiring an application secret or a placement event.

Concrete case: a machine has a declared running-at-delivery service, no application secret will be placed, and the service is stopped at the final delivery check.

Reading A: the new temporal exception applies because no placement has happened. The lifecycle failure is not a finding, although the lifecycle requirement still prevents delivery. This leaves the no-finding/non-delivered state unexplained by ARC-17's delivery/handover rule.

Reading B: the exception is scoped to workflows with a pending placement. For a machine needing no placement, the final check creates the ordinary lifecycle finding and prevents delivery.

The owner accepted the unconditional exception before placement; the decision log does not identify the transition for workflows with no placement. Do not choose a reading in implementation. Recommended clarification: confirm B and state explicitly when final lifecycle checking applies to a workflow that contains no placement. After the answer, amend ARC-17 and CNF-53 together, preserving actual non-lifecycle findings and the post-placement lifecycle gate. Add the no-placement/stopped-service conformance case. Until then this question blocks final specification signoff, not acceptance that the requested sentence was transcribed correctly.

title: The formal companion: the specification gates and the five modules of ADR-0032's inventory
description:
## Problem Statement

The specification has 31 decision records, nine topic files with stable identifiers, and a
conformance checklist that gates an implementation which does not yet exist. It has no gate of
its own: nothing refuses a dangling identifier, a citation that misquotes its target, a
requirement no conformance item exercises, or a renumbering — and the overview records that
"two renumberings have already cost review rounds spent re-verifying what pointed where". Nor
does anything check what a rule *implies* rather than what it *cites*. On 2026-09-16 a review
(`lean-01.md`) found four such defects that every reader had passed: `SEC-1` and `SEC-5` gave
the SSH key two different owners; the relay protocol's summary named an ordering the protocol
does not have; the delivery declaration's presence rule contradicted its own field table; and
`STA-8`'s per-call barrier was evadable by any caller that mints call ids, which every model
does. Each was consistent sentence by sentence and wrong in consequence.

The owner's decision (ADR-0032) is that the corpus's precise semantics — allocation,
declaration presence, relay admission, dispatch and the unresolved barrier, host-pin lifecycle
— are carried as a **formal companion**: Lean definitions and theorems under `tools/formal/`,
on provisiond-spec's ADR-0025 by reference, with the historical traps retained as executable
**witnesses**, and that the implementation is compared against the companion through
**witness files** it emits. The decision is recorded; nothing of it exists in the tree.

## Solution

Land the specification gates and the formal companion in the order ADR-0032 fixes, one
vertical slice per landing, each behind `tools/check-all.sh` with a CI negative control per
check.

First the scaffold (TASKS T30): the seven specification gates ported from provisiond-spec and
adapted to this corpus's shapes, the Lean package under a `TauWeb` namespace with the
`@[req]` attribute, the axiom gate and the index it emits, the Nix shell that pins Lean, and
this repository's withdrawn-identifier table. Then module 1, allocation (T31), with the first
witness file and the emission gate that holds it to the companion's output. Then declaration
presence and meaning, relay admission, dispatch and the unresolved barrier, and the host-pin
lifecycle, each landing as theorems over every input, decided witnesses for the retained
traps, a refused-and-admitted pair for every guard a dated amendment added, and a witness
file.

Authority follows ADR-0032: a formalized clause's home is its tagged declaration; the
requirement keeps its identifier, its MUST, its rationale and its retained traps; the Markdown
stays authoritative for every clause until a rendering gate covers it, and no rendering gate
is ported until there is a table to render. A theorem is never conformance, and nothing in the
inventory gates the first stage.

## User Stories

1. As a spec author, I want a dangling identifier, a duplicate, a gap in a namespace and a
   reference to an ADR that does not exist refused on every push, so that the renumbering
   cost the overview records is paid never again.
2. As a spec author, I want a quoted attribution to a requirement whose body does not contain
   the quote refused, so that "`X` says" is checkable and not an assertion.
3. As a spec author, I want the count of requirements exercised by at least one conformance
   item ratcheted against a recorded baseline, so that the corpus cannot grow faster than its
   checklist without someone saying why.
4. As a spec author, I want a duty assigned to another requirement's subject refused when that
   requirement's own text names none of the machinery, so that a fence protecting an
   operator's machine cannot silently not exist.
5. As a spec author, I want every JSON example and every Mermaid diagram in the corpus parsed,
   so that a fixture with a placeholder or a diagram broken in source is a red gate rather than
   a browser surprise.
6. As a spec author, I want the identifier gate's first run to write this repository's
   withdrawn-identifier table — the retired `SEC-5` rows, `STG-8`, and whatever else it finds
   — so that an old citation still resolves and a gap is a tombstone rather than a mystery.
7. As a spec author, I want every gate run by one script, unpiped, with each exit status
   captured directly, so that green means every gate passed and not that the last one did.
8. As a spec author, I want the ported gates adapted to this corpus's shapes — tiered `CNF`
   items, `docs/design/` JSON, `STA-22a`-style suffixed identifiers — and shown to read what
   they claim to read, so that a port that scans nothing is not a green check.
9. As a spec author, I want a rule I amend to break a theorem when the amendment contradicts a
   property the corpus claims, so that the contradiction is found before review rather than
   by it.
10. As a spec author, I want every "*what this requirement used to say*" paragraph in the
    inventory's clauses kept as an executable witness, so that none of those traps can be
    re-laid without a red build.
11. As a spec author, I want every guard a dated amendment added to be a parameter of the
    module that carries it, with the bad trace refused with the guard and admitted without it,
    so that a proof is never decoration.
12. As a spec author, I want the allocation identity to be a distinct structure of seed epoch,
    derivation version, role family and index, so that two allocations cannot share an
    identity by a type error I never see.
13. As a spec author, I want a failed or destroyed allocation to keep its index as a tombstone
    and no wraparound to exist, proved over every input, so that `STA-22`'s one-index-two-
    machines trap is unrepresentable.
14. As a spec author, I want a seed restored from a stale sheet to use listed identities and
    allocate none until Replace, with that guard a parameter, so that `STA-22b`'s 2026-09-09
    amendment has its refused-and-admitted pair.
15. As a spec author, I want a successful allocate-create-destroy-allocate trace as a witness,
    so that the allocator is not safe merely by refusing everything.
16. As a spec author, I want the declaration's field table to be a total function whose
    totality is decided, so that a field added without its row fails the build, and *presence*
    and *meaning* to be separate types, so that "empty means nothing to check" cannot be
    written for a field where empty means "nothing may".
17. As a spec author, I want the relay's two orderings — no dial before the AUTH is accepted,
    no application byte before OK — to be two theorems, and the destination pipeline to be
    proved to hand the dialer only the validated numeric address, so that this week's
    shorthand defect and a hostname re-entering the dialer are both witnesses.
18. As a spec author, I want harness knowledge and external state to be two types in the
    dispatch module, so that a theorem about the first can never be read as speaking for the
    second.
19. As a spec author, I want `STA-24`'s barrier proved as a derivation over the journal —
    an intent with no terminal record, keyed on the approved machine entry — so that it
    survives replay and session succession by construction and not by an event a crash could
    lose.
20. As a spec author, I want the same destructive action under a new call id, a second
    allocation index for the same approved entry, a planned reset offered after a failed
    append, a `boot_id` change read as success, a resolution observed but its append failed,
    and a disposition read as unrestricted dispatch, each as a negative witness with the
    parameter whose removal admits it.
21. As a spec author, I want `STG-4`'s confirmation predicates and their absence of a negative
    form in the dispatch module, so that "the reset did not happen" can only ever arrive as a
    disposition.
22. As a spec author, I want a disposition modelled as a terminal record of its own kind with
    the outcome unknown, so that the barrier stays one derivation and a disposed call is not an
    open one.
23. As a spec author, I want the host-pin lifecycle to distinguish a rescue pin, per boot, from
    an installed pin, per machine, and to admit an installed pin only from the harness's own
    `ready_to_reset` job, so that a pin from model text and a rescue pin reused across boots
    are both witnesses.
24. As a spec author, I want vendor behaviour, the browser's storage semantics and the
    aggregator honouring a request to appear as named hypotheses on the theorems that depend
    on them, so that a signature shows what was assumed and the companion declares no axiom.
25. As a spec author, I want the companion to emit a witness file per module — its tagged
    witnesses and the bounded enumeration its decided properties close over — with a gate
    refusing a committed file that differs from the emission, so that I never maintain the
    file by hand.
26. As a spec author, I want the bound stated once, in the declaration the theorem and the
    emitter share, and rendered into the file, so that the file's bound and the theorem's
    bound cannot differ.
27. As a spec author, I want a witness file to carry events with provenance and the expected
    outcome at every step, and each refused-and-admitted pair whole and marked, so that a
    core which dispatches early and arrives at the right state does not pass.
28. As a spec author, I want a witness file to carry no `CNF` identifier, no claim about
    external state, no timer value and no key material, so that the file cannot be counted as
    coverage, cannot be read as evidence about a machine, and needs no secrets warning.
29. As a reviewer reading a landing without memory of the session, I want the emitted index
    to say which requirement each declaration formalizes, so that I can check a declaration
    against the sentence it claims to carry.
30. As a reviewer, I want every tagged proof to rest on `propext`, `Classical.choice` and
    `Quot.sound` only, with `sorryAx`, a project axiom and `native_decide` each refused by the
    gate, so that a green build means what it says.
31. As a reviewer, I want each check to have a CI control that breaks the thing it guards and
    asserts the red came from that check, so that a red for the wrong reason is never taken
    as evidence.
32. As a reviewer, I want a backticked `TauWeb.*` name in a document resolved against the
    emitted index, so that a renamed declaration cannot leave a dangling citation.
33. As a reviewer, I want a weakened theorem statement or a strengthened premise to be
    reviewed as a semantic change like any other, so that a proof never becomes complete
    because the theorem became weaker.
34. As CI, I want the formal gate to build and gate in the same job as the textual gates,
    under the same Nix shell a developer uses, so that there is one toolchain definition and
    a missing toolchain is a red gate rather than a skipped one.
35. As CI, I want a module under `TauWeb/` that the umbrella module does not import refused,
    so that a proof file nobody reads is not a green check.
36. As CI, I want a gate over an empty index refused, so that a gate over nothing is not a
    gate.
37. As the implementation's author, I want the witness files under `docs/design/` beside the
    credential vectors, read from the pinned tree by tests and never compiled in, so that no
    Lean enters the implementation's toolchain and ADR-0031's boundary stays where it is.
38. As the implementation's author, I want the witness file to supply requests as a model
    would send them and never an already-correct resource key, so that the request-to-entry
    mapping is what my comparison tests.
39. As the implementation's author, I want a conformance item to be able to cite a witness
    file as one input and never as the only evidence it accepts, so that module 1 does not
    gate the first live rehearsal.
40. As the owner, I want the inventory built in the order that lets each module be true when
    it lands — allocation, declaration, relay, dispatch, pins — so that no module proves a
    false requirement to save time.
41. As the owner, I want Mathlib added only in a commit naming the theorem that cannot close
    without it, so that the dependency is never carried by default.
42. As the owner, I want no word *model* in the companion's names, docstrings or glossary
    entries, so that the weights and the companion are never one word.
43. As the owner, I want the rendering gate ported only when the first table exists to render,
    so that the glossary never describes an artifact that does not exist.
44. As the owner, I want each landing reviewed on two axes — against `AGENTS.md`, ADR-0032 and
    the glossary, and against the cited requirement sentences — before the next starts, so
    that the companion is reviewed alongside the specification rather than becoming a parallel
    research project.

## Implementation Decisions

**Placement and authority** (ADR-0032). `tools/` is the one carve-out from "specification
only": the gates that check the specification, and under `tools/formal/` the companion. A
formalized clause's home is its Lean declaration tagged `@[req "STA-22b"]`, one declaration
one identifier; the Markdown keeps identifier, MUST, rationale and retained traps and renders
the clause; until a rendering gate covers a clause the Markdown stays authoritative. No `CNF`
identifier appears under `tools/formal/` or in a witness file, and the coverage gate counts
nothing from the companion.

**The scaffold, ported from provisiond-spec and adapted.** `check-all.sh` running, in order:
the formal gate (build, axiom policy, index, witness-file emission), identifiers, fixtures,
obligations, coverage, citations. Each gate's exit status captured directly. The namespace
table becomes this corpus's: `OVR`, `ARC`, `CHN`, `STA`, `SEC`, `TRU`, `STG`, `CNF`, `OPN`,
with suffixed identifiers (`STA-22a`, `CHN-R1`, `SEC-T1`, `SEC-CLAIM`) admitted by the
identifier pattern. The conformance parser reads this corpus's `- [ ] **CNF-n · TIER**` item
shape and its applicability table. The fixture gate reads JSON under `docs/design/` and every
Mermaid block in the topic files, ADRs and profiles. The withdrawn-identifier table lives in
`README.md` under a "Requirement conventions" section the corpus does not yet have, seeded by
the gate's first run: the retired `SEC-5` rows 8 and 13, `STG-8`, `ARC-23`/`SEC-T*` pointers
(kept, not withdrawn), and whatever else the sequence check finds. `AGENTS.md` is provisiond's
with the Lean paragraph and this corpus's file names; `docs/agents/` holds the tracker, label
and domain-doc conventions.

**The Lean package.** `tools/formal/` with `lean-toolchain` pinned to the same Lean as
provisiond-spec, `lakefile.toml` with the library, the `gate` executable and the `witnesses`
executable as default targets, no dependencies. `TauWeb/Req.lean` carries the attribute;
`Gate.lean` collects axioms for every tagged declaration, refuses anything outside the three
standard axioms, refuses `native_decide` outside `TauWeb.Explore` by the axiom's shape, refuses
an empty index, and prints one JSON object per tagged declaration. `TauWeb.lean`'s imports are
the module list and the wrapper refuses a module missing from it. One module per inventory
row: `Allocation`, `Declaration`, `Relay`, `Dispatch`, `Pins`, plus `Types` for the shared
identities and `Witnesses` for the retained traps. Identities are structures, never aliases.

**The Nix shell.** `flake.nix` on provisiond-spec's, pinned to the nixpkgs revision that
caches the chosen Lean; `nix flake check` runs the same gates. CI enters the shell and runs
`check-all.sh`, then one negative-control step per gate, each against a scratch copy, each
asserting the failure came from the check it targets.

**Module 1, allocation** (`STA-22`, `STA-22a`, `STA-22b`, the credential format's index rules).
An allocation identity is seed epoch, derivation version, role family, index. The journal owns
next-unused per family and the allocated entries with tombstones; reserve is durable before
any external effect; a failed or destroyed allocation keeps its index; indices are monotonic in
`0 … 2^31−1` with no wraparound; a seed restored from a sheet or store uses listed identities
and allocates none until Replace, that guard a parameter. Theorems: no two allocations share an
identity, over every trace; a restored seed's allocation is refused with the guard and admitted
without it; a successful allocate-create-destroy-allocate trace as a witness; exhaustion refuses
rather than wraps. The role-index mapping of the credential format is a closed table whose
totality is decided.

**Module 2, declaration presence and meaning** (`ARC-39`, the declaration document).
Presence is one type — missing, unspecified, specified — for every field; meaning is one
function per field; the field table is a total function whose totality is decided. Theorem: no
path reaches delivered while a required field is unspecified or missing; an empty inbound list
with any listener is a finding while an empty restriction list is not. Witness: the presence
rule as it read until 2026-09-16.

**Module 3, relay admission** (`CHN-15`, `CHN-16`, `CHN-16a`, the relay protocol). The
handshake as a state machine with `AuthAccepted` distinct from `OkSent`; the check order of
step 3 as a total function; the destination pipeline as parse, normalize, classify, dial with
the dialer's argument the classified numeric address by type. Theorems: no dial before
`AuthAccepted`; no application byte before `OkSent`; a hostname never reaches the dialer; a
replayed AUTH fails on its challenge. Witness: "no dial before OK" as one invariant.

**Module 4, dispatch and the unresolved barrier** (`STA-3`, `STA-4`, `STA-7`, `STA-8`,
`STA-24`, `SEC-12`, `STA-20b`, `STG-4`). Harness knowledge and external state as two types; the
journal as a list of events; intents with resource, kind, session and approval; terminal
records including dispositions; `unresolved r` derived; observations carrying provenance as a
type (adapter read, pin-checked handshake, job record, notify event, model text); the resource
key as a parameter (approved entry versus call id); the reset offer's precondition as a
parameter; the observation lattice with ended below succeeded. The principal theorem: an effect
is dispatched only if its intent and approval are durable, the binding still holds, the
approved facts are what is dispatched, and no unresolved call names its resource except under
a durable disposition naming that continuation. Companion theorems: replay yields the same
unresolved set; only an adapter-read or pin-checked observation confirms a cloud-plane intent;
a failed append leaves the barrier standing. Witnesses: the six in ADR-0032's inventory row.
Robot's predicates have no negative transition; "not happened" is only a disposition event.

**Module 5, host-pin lifecycle** (`SEC-11`, `CHN-R1`, `ARC-43`). A rescue pin per boot, an
installed pin per machine; a pin's admission source as a type; connection admitted only against
a pin for the right machine and phase. Theorems: a rescue pin is never reused across boots; an
installed pin comes only from the `ready_to_reset` job's captured output; no connection before
`/rescue/last` fills. Witnesses: each of those three, negated.

**Witness files** (ADR-0032, "How the implementation is compared"). `lake exe witnesses`
emits one JSON file per module: schema version, module, bound; per trace the `TauWeb.*`
declarations it came from, the guard parameters as assumptions, events in from a closed
vocabulary with provenance, and the expected outcome at every step as a projection in the
requirements' vocabulary. Committed as `docs/design/<module>-witnesses-v1.json`; a
specification gate refuses a committed file that differs from the emission. Each
refused-and-admitted pair appears whole and marked. The emitter refuses to emit a module
whose tagged witnesses it did not reach.

**Vocabulary.** `CONTEXT.md` already carries formal companion, specification gate, witness,
assumption, property, theorem, decided, witness file, bound, companion comparison. Marked
region and any lifecycle-module term are added when the artifacts exist.

## Testing Decisions

The one seam is `tools/check-all.sh` and the exit status of each gate it runs. A good test
breaks one artifact in a scratch copy and requires that gate, and only that gate, to go red
naming the thing it guards; it never tests a Lean declaration or a Python function directly,
and it never asserts on a build's stdout beyond the named failure. A red build for the wrong
reason is not evidence.

Controls, one per check, in CI on every push and runnable locally:

- identifiers: a dangling citation appended; a tier removed from an item that must carry one
  (this corpus keeps tiers, unlike provisiond); a withdrawn identifier reintroduced.
- citations: a quoted phrase its target never contained; a `TauWeb.*` name the index lacks.
- obligations: a duty naming machinery its target never mentions.
- coverage: a requirement appended with no conformance item, above the baseline.
- fixtures: a JSON example with a placeholder; a Mermaid block with a broken edge.
- formal, build: the restored-seed guard's parameter flipped, asserting the unsolved goal is
  in the allocation module; the resource key switched to call id, asserting the refused
  witness fails.
- formal, axiom gate: a `sorry` the build accepts, asserting `sorryAx` in the gate's output;
  a `native_decide` outside `Explore`.
- formal, imports: a module file the umbrella does not import.
- formal, witness files: a committed file edited by hand; a witness the emitter did not reach.

Prior art: provisiond-spec's `ci.yml`, whose negative controls are the shape to copy, and this
corpus's `check-install-disks.py --baseline`, which checks a reviewed pre-fix commit and must
fail. The companion comparison in tau-web-rust is its own test with its own `CNF-3` controls
and is outside this spec.

## Out of Scope

- tau-web-rust: the companion comparison, the Rust core's shape, its `CNF-3` controls, the
  README's `CNF-1`–`CNF-4` mislabel (corrected at the next pin bump).
- The rendering gate and marked regions, until a formalized table exists to render.
- The "later" row of the inventory: attest single-use across restart, exposure reach per
  domain, handoff reach.
- Proving selected Rust against the companion (Aeneas): not adopted, not tracked.
- Mathlib.
- Any change to `07-conformance.md`'s applicability table: nothing here gates the first stage.
- Formalizing briefs, arbitrary shell, or anything about a machine's actual state.

## Further Notes

The two panel records under `docs/review/` dated 2026-09-16 carry the divergences the readers
had on `STA-24` and on the comparison mechanism, and what was taken from each. Three things
they left open are recorded there and are not this spec's to close: whether a Robot reset can
be delayed or dropped, whether the aggregator offers an idempotency key, and the preconditions
for reusing `STG-4`'s installed-pin predicate on a general reset.

provisiond-spec's epic `pv-vwe` and its first closed ticket `pv-vwe.1` are the shape each
landing here follows, including the two-axis review before the next ticket starts. Its
`Claim.lean` is the shape of module 4: distinct identities, "the store committed" and "the
worker learned it committed" as separate facts, the prohibited alternative made definable so it
can be refuted, and the witnesses file holding each historical defect as a `decide`.

title: The rendering gate: marked regions for the two formalized tables
description:
## Parent

tw-formal-companion-nxy.

## What to build

The rendering gate (ADR-0032, "No marked regions yet": "the gate is ported when the first one
exists"), ported from provisiond's `tools/check_regions.py`. Two tables become marked regions:
the field table of `delivery-declaration-v1.md` on `TauWeb.Declaration.row`, and the role table
of `credential-format-v1.md` on `TauWeb.Allocation.row`. Both are `match` regions: their cells
carry prose and conformance citations the companion must never emit, so only the tokens the
declaration determines are compared and the prose beside them stays the document's.

Settled by a six-reader panel over two rounds (Fable, Opus, codex gpt-6-astra, codex gpt-5.6-sol;
`.context/regions-*.md`, `.context/regions2-*.md`).

## Decisions

- **The outcome column.** The delivery table gains a fourth column whose single bold token per
  row the declaration emits: `**number**`, `**flag**`, `**nothing may**`, `**none declared**`,
  `**on re-entry**`, a bijection with `Shape` and `EmptyMeans`. Verified collision-free against
  every token in the existing Value and check cells; never a backticked literal, since `` `1` ``,
  `` `false` ``, `` `true` ``, `` `[]` `` and `` `"none"` `` already appear there. The header is
  never compared, so the column title is free.
- **The role table** gains tokens in all three carried columns and backticked role numbers as
  keys: a bare key emits no token and makes the subsequence check vacuous.
- **Escape-aware cell splitting.** Two Value cells carry `\|`; provisiond's `split("|")` reads
  them as column boundaries and the rows arrive with too many cells, so the gate stops before
  reading a token. Split on backslash parity.
- **Placement.** A region may sit in the requirement its declaration is tagged with, or in a
  document that requirement's body links to. `ARC-39` links the declaration document and
  `STA-22a` the credential format, so the rule is checkable from the Markdown with no hand-kept
  map. The check is directional: other documents linking the same file are irrelevant.
- **Its own index reader.** `check_citations.lean_names()` discards the requirement each
  declaration is tagged with, and this repository exports no requirement-head regex, so the gate
  reads `.lake/index.jsonl` itself and reuses `check_ids.DEF_RE`.
- **One label per refusal class**, each printing a list or `none`. A single label can never count
  two, which voids `check-controls.sh`'s "exactly one finding" contract; the identifier gate's
  eight labels are the house style. No trailing `FAIL:` summary, which would itself count.
- **Emission order.** `lake exe render` runs before the index is written, because this
  repository writes the index only on a green run. Provisiond's order is the opposite and is not
  copied.
- **No `--write`.** Both regions are `match`, which provisiond never rewrites, so the flag would
  ship with nothing to do.
- **Scan set**: root `*.md`, `docs/adr/`, `docs/design/`, `docs/tenants/*/profile.md`. A marker in
  a profile is refused by the placement rule rather than ignored.
- **Kind is an inductive** in Lean, and the Python gate still refuses an unknown kind: the JSON
  file is a boundary between two programs.
- **The emitted region text is checked for a `CNF` identifier**, as the witness gate checks its
  emissions. The prohibition is path-independent.
- The Presence rule stops enumerating fields and names the new column instead ("Cite the list;
  let it hold the number"). The two category explanations and the dated trap stay.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `lake exe render` emits both regions; `tools/check_regions.py` holds each document equal to
  its declaration and runs in `check-all.sh` after the formal gate
- [ ] A control per refusal: drift in each region, a region whose declaration is not indexed, a
  region whose file its requirement does not link, an emitted region no document renders, a
  duplicate region, an unopened and an unclosed marker, a non-table line in a `match` region, an
  unknown kind, and a `CNF` identifier in an emission
- [ ] One control proves an edit one line outside a region stays green
- [ ] ADR-0032's "No marked regions yet" bullet carries the dated sentence and the placement
  rule; `AGENTS.md` and `CONTEXT.md`'s **Formal companion** widen "renders the clause" the same
  way; `CONTEXT.md` gains **Marked region**; `README.md`'s gate prose names the gate
- [ ] The gate's docstring states what it does not catch: a header row, prose contradicting the
  token beside it, and a key token that is a subsequence rather than an exclusive identity
- [ ] Two-axis review applied before the next ticket starts

## Scheduling

Module 3 (`tw-formal-companion-nxy.8`) depends on this ticket. **No sentence in either repository
requires that edge** — all three round-two readers said so explicitly. It is a scheduling call:
the trigger has fired, the gate is cheaper to port before more tables exist, and the tracker's
frontier is worked in id order, so an edge is the only way to say "before module 3".

title: Let the operator end a lost application key's wait by reporting it revoked at its service
description:
After local-store loss with no copy of an application key, `ARC-43` says "Model `exec` across the bound set MUST wait while any known required placement reference is unarmed." That wait ends by a re-arm (`digest_secret` or the local paste) or by a rotation `ARC-17`'s placement gates admit. A reinstall alone ends nothing, and neither does the stop that stands in for a destroy (`ARC-22`). Where the reinstall leaves no file at the recorded path for `digest_secret` to read, and the commands the machine needs after it (its install, or a fix for a finding that refuses placement) are model commands, rotation cannot be reached, and only a paste or the machine's destruction (at LNVPS, the vendor's confirmed deletion, `SEC-5` row 23) ends the wait for them. At stage 2 the other machines' output waits too: `CNF-95(f)` says "With neither, one or both pasted, output on A and B is released only after both."

Add a per-placement operator act, taken after the operator revokes the key at its service. It is journaled before it takes effect; it lifts no `STA-20` or `STA-24` restriction and authorizes no retry; it ends that placement's required reference and its live listing (`SEC-5` rows 12 and 23, `SEC-6`, `TRU-E12`), moving it to history labelled operator-reported. Ending the reference also ends the scan for that value, and ADR-0050 rejected "Release the other machines' output without the disposed machine's references"; the act's ADR says why a key revoked at its service changes that. The sheet carries it (`STA-16`), and a sheet exported before it restores the wait. It is not called "retired", which pins already use. A missing file, a changed pin or a new installation never produces it. `CNF-95` gains: a reinstall alone ends nothing; acting on P1 alone still waits on P2; a failed append; replay; an older sheet's Restore invents no report. The sheet record fits the pre-deployment version-3 payload (`docs/design/credential-format-v1.md`) only until stage-1 sheets exist; after that it needs a format version (`STA-22a`).

Due before stage 2 (`STG-22`) opens. Earlier, before stage 1 completes, if a fresh LNVPS catalogue image fails the fixed lockdown checks of T42's checklist.

title: Does a job still running on an installed system hold the next box-plane command to that machine?
description:
## The question

While a job record shows a box-plane command still running on an installed system, does the
harness worker hold the next box-plane command the model requests for that machine, or does it
only decline to re-run the dropped command?

## What the text says

- `STA-20`: "On reconnect the session reads that record rather than guessing — exit code present
  means finished, the command's own process alive means wait."
- `STA-20b`, for rescue: "A reconnect checks this record before issuing more work; a still-running
  job is waited on, including during partitioning." `CNF-86` tests it "including when the model
  requests the work under a new command id".
- `CNF-40`, for the installed system: the returning session "waits on the job record rather than
  launching a second one". It says nothing of a new command id.
- `STA-24`: "box-plane commands may be unresolved together, as `STA-20`'s tracked jobs are."
- ADR-0022: "a still-running command re-run concurrently is the corruption case the whole
  question exists for."

## Readings

- A: while one of a machine's jobs is seen running, the next box-plane command to that machine
  waits. A model that requests a dropped install again under a new call id waits instead of
  running it beside the first.
- B: only the dropped call is waited on. A fresh model request is dispatched, and converging is
  the brief's: `ARC-10` says "Convergence is therefore an authoring rule, not a subsystem".

The implementation built B with its job records and holds the question as twr-ggw.69. The answer
decides what a session does at its start and at re-entry. Item "**CNF-40 · BLOCKING**" says
"This is the corruption case, which is why it blocks", and `07-conformance.md`'s "Stage 1:
required" row lists items 39–44 and says "Interrupted resume (`STG-12`) is carried here by
items 37, 39, 40 and 54–56".

## Closes when

The text says which reading holds on the installed system, in `STA-20` or `CNF-40`.
