title: Define the installation target and no-pin acceptance boundary, including reinstall
description:
# Define the installation target and no-pin acceptance boundary

## Question

When a catalogue bootstrap image differs from the distribution to be installed, when must the operator fix that installation target and accept its no-pin mode? May acceptance follow binding if it precedes every contact/act it governs? If the intended distribution or installation changes, which operator act authorizes the change and which acceptance applies? For a pinned installation with no no-pin acceptance record, must a separate approved target/association fact exist, which operation supplies it, and does absence or conflict refuse the install? A requested distribution naming a pin and an operator-approved association are distinct facts; this is open condition P1-C1, not a decided exemption.

## Established boundary

SEC-14 says "A mode is accepted by the session that does what it governs, before doing it." ARC-25 says "Installing a distribution the bundle carries no pin for is an acceptable weaker mode (`SEC-14`): the operator chooses it up front, from what the bundle lacks, and the machine is recorded and shown as **unpinned** from then on." ADR-0035 says "Artifact pinning stays BLOCKING wherever a pin exists; what the operator may choose, up front, is a distribution that has none."

These sentences do not unambiguously settle the proposed later window or a target-change act. The implementation currently accepts the mode at initial binding and describes that window as an implementation reading. The pending repair names the intended distribution and retains that earlier window; it supplies no blanket pin bypass. Historical acceptance replay and new installation under a newer bundle are separate cases.

## Answer must demonstrate

- State the acceptance boundary and target-changing act, or explicitly refuse later acceptance/target amendment; distinguish catalogue image, intended installed distribution, acceptance history and actual installation state.
- Cover pinned distribution, unpinned distribution, failed-pin fallback, changed target, and an acceptance predating a bundle that adds a pin. New installation must not inherit a permanent exemption from old history.
- Give conformance cases that distinguish the chosen timing/target rule, including refusal before any governed act when its prerequisites are absent. Include a pinned install with no no-pin association and one with a recorded conflicting target; state the chosen result and its authority. Never bypass an applicable pin.
- Land the normative answer with SEC-14/ARC-25 and retain ADR-0035's boundary; update any formalized clauses and their prose together where affected.

Reinstall's requirement to accept afresh is tracked separately by implementation tickets `twr-ggw.81` and `twr-ggw.45` in `douglaz/tau-web-rust`; this question must not replace it. No live observation or new runtime reproduction is claimed.

## Reinstall authority and history — part of this question

SEC-14 says:

> A mode is accepted by the session that does what it governs, before doing it.

> An installation with no artifact pin and a first contact from a jump host are the machine's history: every later set that includes the machine is shown them at binding and restates them, and accepts them again only for a reinstall, which is a new installation and a new first contact (`CHN-R6`).

STG-20 says:

> That separately approved destructive reinstall opens a new installation when it is **dispatched**: the reset into rescue on a dedicated server, or the vendor's reinstall call at LNVPS.

> Choosing it or recording its disposition does not move that boundary.

The required fresh acceptance is settled. Clarify the remaining successor contract: which independently approved fact identifies the target installation/distribution for pinned and unpinned dispatch; whether acceptance may precede intent; what prevents reuse after cancellation, changed target or ended session; how predecessor history remains standing/presented after a pinned successor; and who accepts an unpinned reinstall from a deterministic flow outside a session.

Competing complete proposal families, neither adopted:

- Dispatch-coupled: a typed approved target explicitly identifies the successor distribution/installation for either pin status; missing/conflicting approved facts refuse. Required no-pin acceptance is durable in the matching dispatch intent. Cancelled proposals create no reusable acceptance or new installation. Keep every earlier dispatched installation's history visible/restated and show current installation status separately. Explicitly decide its standing projection; do not silently remove required restatement.
- Prior-record: an independently approved target association precedes acceptance for the exact session/set, allocation/machine, intended installation/distribution, bundle and proposal. Ended session, cancellation and any changed target invalidate use before dispatch. Acceptance alone never opens an installation; unused acceptance is labelled separately from dispatched history. A pinned target uses an expressly approved target fact despite having no no-pin acceptance. Historical disclosure/restatement remains mandatory; resolve its standing projection explicitly.

For either family, choose the outside-session acceptor rule explicitly: require a session bound to the machine before no-pin dispatch, or amend SEC-14 to permit a named deterministic operator-flow card to accept for a defined machine/set with the same durability/history obligations. Refusing a required recovery route while waiting is not assumed to be specification-compliant.

Discriminating traces: acceptance then cancellation then a later same-target proposal; session ending before send; changed distribution/bundle; historical unpinned then pinned successor then later binding/placement; pinned target without a no-pin record; opening-screen recovery outside a session; durable intent with lost response. Keep applicable pins enforced, failed-pin fallback prohibited, installation/pin retirement at dispatch only, replay non-dispatching and vendor confirmation separate. Resolve the smallest remaining differences through technical confirmation before presenting any complete behavior choice for adoption.

Category: bug. State: needs-triage. Priority: P2. No behavior answer, implementation readiness or closure is implied by filing this question.

title: Robot rescue rekey moves the installation id but leaves the root's label stale; its ordinal may be unknown
description:
## The gap

`STA-17` says "If the old seed or an index is missing, direct re-entry and pass revocation
cannot finish. Robot machines can still be rekeyed through vendor-authenticated rescue
(`STA-15`)". `STA-22b` says "With no sheet, or for machines missing from a stale sheet, Robot
recovery installs keys from a fresh seed through vendor-authenticated rescue and re-reads host
pins; it does not guess old indices".

On that path the machine takes an index under the fresh seed, so the shown installation id's
machine component moves (`STG-20`). Replace's relabel job covers a dedicated machine reached by
direct re-entry. It does not cover this path. A root rekeyed this way keeps a label that no
longer equals the shown id. The install brief recognises only a label equal to the shown id as
its own installation, so the next return to rescue on that machine reads the machine's own root
as a predecessor and can steer toward erasing it.

## What is open

- **The ordinal.** The label is `<machine>-<n>`. With no sheet, or a stale one, the journal may
  hold no installation for the machine: `CHN-R7` says a non-destructive recovery "does not open
  an installation", and the credential format says Replace's migration "does not restart at
  zero". Nothing defines `n` here. Either a rule supplies it (for example from a readable,
  well-formed old root label), or nothing is written and the machine stays unmigrated until it
  is known.
- **The order.** No connection authenticated by the old key exists on this path, but the rescue
  ceremony ends in the installed system, so a connection authenticated by the new key can still
  be confirmed before a relabel. Whether the relabel then runs in the installed system or from
  rescue, and when the machine counts as migrated, is open.
- **The job.** `ARC-43`'s job list has no rescue rekey job yet.

## When it must be settled

Dedicated path only (cloud machines are destroyed and recreated). It must be settled before a
dedicated-server path is offered to an operator, which no stage before the third does; it sits
beside `CNF-84`'s Robot rescue case in `07-conformance.md`'s dedicated row.

title: Define the single-machine session route to a different entry after definitive failure

# Define the single-machine session route to a different entry after definitive failure

## Question

When the sole machine allocation of a stage-1 session definitively fails, can that same live session order a different newly approved entry? How is that consistent with retained bound-set membership and the single-machine stage-1 constraint? If it needs a successor session, what ends the old one and authorizes the new one?

## Established boundary

SEC-1 says "No machine leaves a set while the session is alive — what the model has read from it stays in the context that commands the rest."

STA-24 says "A different approved entry is independent, and creating it while a sibling is unresolved is permitted under its own approval, whose card shows the unresolved sibling and that it may be billing."

The unresolved-sibling rule supplies neither an exception to session membership nor an automatic route after definitive failure. A different entry and a new allocation index are not themselves authority to grow or shrink a single-machine session. The pending bounded repair adds no such route.

## Answer must demonstrate

- Specify the permissible stage-1 route, including old session membership, any required session end/successor, approval of the new entry and retained failed-allocation history.
- Distinguish same-entry replacement from a different entry, unresolved sibling from definitive failure, and stage-1 single-machine sessions from stage-2 set growth. Preserve any profile independence-bound constraint.
- Supply conformance refusal for an unauthorized added entry and admission for the chosen operator-approved route; a fresh index must not bypass the boundary.
- Land the answer with SEC-1/ARC-15 and the stage-1 applicability owners, updating affected formalized clauses and prose together.

No live vendor call or runtime reproduction is claimed. This is a specification question, not an implementation instruction to add automatic retries or discard a failed member.

Category: bug. State: needs-triage. Priority: P2. No behavior answer, implementation readiness or closure is implied by filing this question.

title: Under an untyped vendor scope, does a destructive hold refuse harness-started jobs?
description:
`STA-24` pauses "a box-plane command to any machine of the session's bound set at that vendor" while a call under the scope is open or unresolved, and says "a continuation that continues ends the pause and a destructive one does not (*the hold*, below)"; the hold "keeps the model's box-plane commands to the machines of the session's bound set at that vendor stopped until the operator replaces it". Whether a harness-composed job (`digest_secret`, `delivery_reboot`, `replace_root_label`) is refused under the hold is unsettled, and ADR-0050 stops every box-plane job "whoever starts it" for a machine's destructive disposition.

ADR-0038 records: "Abandonment still has no typed destroy to run at such a vendor, and `ARC-21` and `ARC-22` now hand the act to the operator; while a disposition naming abandonment or a destructive reinstall stands on the scope, `STA-24` holds every further call under it and the model's box-plane commands to the set's machines at that vendor until the operator replaces the disposition (ADR-0044)."

title: Does a destroyed machine free the other machines' held output?
description:
`SEC-5` row 23 ends a placed secret's scan key and reference at the machine's destruction: "Until rotation, machine destruction (at LNVPS, the vendor's confirmed deletion, not the stop that stands in for a destroy, `ARC-22`) or local-store loss; re-arm replaces it with a fresh key/reference".

`CNF-95(f)` says "With neither, one or both pasted, output on A and B is released only after both."

ADR-0050 rejected "Release the other machines' output without the disposed machine's references" because "`SEC-5` says "Unscanned bytes MUST be withheld"; a secret copied onto another machine would go unscanned."

No text says whether M's confirmed destruction (at LNVPS, the vendor's confirmed deletion) releases A and B's withheld output, or whether their later output is still scanned for M's secret.

Bound sets of more than one machine are stage 2 (`STG-22`).

title: Does anything hold a restored machine whose pre-loss command may still be running?
description:
## Decision — journal-only, 2026-11-01

The owner chose journal-only protection. Add no recovery check or hold for commands absent from the restored journal. New work after recovery, including Replace's model-free key migration, may overlap an earlier command the restored journal does not record. Intents without terminal records that a backup does retain still hold under the existing journal-derived rules. Other admission checks and standing restrictions remain in force.

## Why this issue exists

A machine can keep running a command after the phone loses the journal that recorded its send. A sheet contains no outstanding-call record. An imported local-store backup differs from total journal loss: it may retain some unresolved intents, while omitting later sends. The original question's claim that nothing journaled holds every restored machine was too broad for that backup case.

`STA-24` states "The barrier is a fact of the journal — an intent with no terminal record" and "What this rule cannot reach is a journal that is lost with the phone: `STA-14` states that transcripts are gone, and a recovery sheet is not an outstanding-call record." `STA-20` records jobs "on persistent disk (`/var/lib/tau-web/jobs`, root-only)" and says "On the installed system the files survive a reboot". Those surviving machine records do not recreate a lost journal intent.

`STA-21` states "The job record is machine-reported and advisory." Enumeration cannot reveal commands that left no record, prove completeness against a hostile machine or reconstruct approvals. This limit must not be presented as a new concurrency guarantee.

## Triage outcome

Astra and Sol recommended a bounded recovery guard. Opus recommended an operator-cancellable advisory wait. Fable was a missing seat because of its usage limit; Grok was a missing seat because of HTTP 402 balance exhaustion. The owner explicitly rejected those recommendations in favor of journal-only. The structured brief in this issue's comments records the decision, the still-binding constraints and the acceptance criteria.

## Closes when

The owning `STA-20` command-hold text and `STA-24` lost-journal limit explicitly describe this boundary, including overlap during Replace, without bypassing any retained unresolved intent or standing restriction. Preserve advisory evidence, existing collection and all other admission rules. The amendment must not weaken any existing theorem, gate, requirement or assumption boundary. No recovery guard, advisory wait or new dispatch exception is part of this outcome.

Found by the 2026-10-18 grill (tw-k12). The issue remains open for the bounded specification clarification; no normative amendment or integrated result is claimed by triage.

title: CNF-109's admission from the job-read and attest routes at stage 1, which has neither
description:
## The question

`CNF-109` is in the stage-1 required row ("109–110") with no carve-out. Two of its sentences need
a route stage 1 does not have: a new job-read pin needs the dedicated path's rescue job, and a new
attest pin needs the attest route:

- "a new valid published, job-read, or unused eligible attest introduction can pin under its own

- "A consumed attest introduction stays consumed."

attest attempt, which only the attest route can make.

its admission of an unused attest introduction, and a consumed introduction staying consumed, are
the attest row's, as item 23's attest-window case already is. Stage 1 keeps the cases against
earlier job-read and attest pins, on pins a Restore brings in.

The implementation's companion comparison of `pins-witnesses-v4.json` leaves the 16 witnesses
holding an `attest` step (and 2246 enumerated traces) unreplayed at stage 1 until this is
answered, and its stage-1 admission record lists them by name as pending.

The stage-1 row, or `CNF-109`, says where these two sentences apply, on the spec's main.

title: LNVPS operations have no confirmation predicate (restart, stop, renewal-off, reinstall, deletion)
description:
## The gap

`STA-24`: "Evidence is the observation the operation's own reconciliation contract admits — for
Robot, `STG-4`'s predicates". `STG-4` and the rules after it define those predicates for Robot only.
No requirement defines the observation that confirms any LNVPS operation: the typed restart, the stop
that stands in for a destroy, renewal-off, or the vendor's reinstall call.

So at LNVPS each of those calls stays unresolved until the operator disposes of it, and while one
that changes what the machine is running (`STA-24`) is unresolved, box-plane dispatch to the
machine stays stopped. Duties resting on the missing contract:
- `ARC-43`: the opted-in delivery restart, "with its own vendor confirmation under `STA-24`";
  "Until that confirmation, box-plane dispatch stays stopped." (the boot-identity read is never
  the restart's confirmation).
- `STA-24`: "At LNVPS renewal-off waits for the stop's confirmation".
- `STA-24`: the reinstall continuation at LNVPS is dispatched at "the vendor's reinstall call";
  its confirmation closes the restriction's successor barrier.
- The implementation's LNVPS tickets (stop and renewal-off; reinstall, "confirmed only by the
  predicate the spec pin carries").

## The question

For each of the four operations, what observation — from LNVPS's machine status read
(`GET /api/v1/vm/{id}`, `VmStatus`), its published host keys, or a box-plane read where `STA-24`
allows one — confirms it, what is merely "ended", and what leaves it unresolved? Ground it in the
2026-10-08 LNVPS research and the 2026-10-11 phase B observations.

Found by the 2026-10-16 contradiction pass over branch docs/grill-1015.

The vendor's deletion of a stopped machine needs a confirming observation beside those of the four harness operations. `SEC-5` rows 12 and 23 count it as the machine's destruction at LNVPS: "the vendor's confirmed deletion, not the stop that stands in for a destroy"; that deletion observation is owed here too. The starting fact in `docs/findings/2026-10-11-lnvps-phase-b.md` is "A stop (`PATCH …/stop`) left the machine `stopped` and still listed, with `deleting_on` one day after the expiry (the grace may lengthen with the subscription's age; it was read at day 0)." No deletion has been observed. The observation has to work for a machine whose vendor key went with a retired or missing seed (`STA-17`); without one, that machine's placed secrets stay listed for good.
close_reason: T50 specified in STA-5, STA-24, STG-21/STG-21a and CNF-112: narrow exact-call receipts, unique-match order reconciliation, renewal/reinstall/deletion reads and account verification/reissue. ADR-0042 and TRU-E1 record accepted administrative-transfer risk and the deferred reappearance billing-display gap. Lost-key duties remain; no operator-carried evidence path. Specification closure only; no live deletion or implementation claim.

title: Does a destructive disposition stop a box-plane job the harness starts on its own?
description:
## The question

While a disposition naming a destructive reinstall or abandonment stands on a machine, is a
box-plane job the harness starts on its own (`delivery_reboot`, `digest_secret`, the delivery
check's harness-composed reads, `replace_root_label`) refused, or dispatched?

## What the text says

- `STA-24`: "the harness worker MUST refuse the model's box-plane commands to that machine,
  whatever the disposed call was. A harness-owned job the model requests (`ARC-43`) is one of
  them". Harness-initiated jobs are not named.
- `STA-24`: "a disposed box-plane command restricts only what an unresolved box-plane command
  bars", and "Box-plane dispatch to the machine is governed by `STA-20` and `STA-20b`, not by
  this rule". `STA-20`'s hold (2026-10-18, ADR-0048) is released by any disposition, so it is
  not part of a disposition's reach.
- `STA-24`: "a disposed create, activation or key registration bars nothing on the box plane".
- ADR-0044 rejected "A destructive continuation adds nothing beyond what the disposed call
  barred" because "A stray command would pre-empt the reinstall the operator chose".

`TauWeb.Dispatch` follows the text: under a standing destructive reinstall disposition of a
command, a `deliveryReboot` request is dispatched, stays unresolved, and its barrier refuses
the reinstall's rescue activation until its boot change is collected.

## Readings

- A: the destructive stop covers every box-plane job, harness-initiated ones included; only
  reads and the collection of job records pass.
- B: as written today; a harness-initiated job runs under a destructive continuation and can
  pre-empt the reinstall.

## Closes when

`STA-24` says which reading holds for harness-initiated jobs, and `TauWeb.Dispatch` agrees.
close_reason: STA-24 stops every box-plane job; ARC-43 paste at once; STA-17; CNF-95/CNF-110; TauWeb.Dispatch.stops; ADR-0050

title: No check reads where the abandonment continuation is dispatched (TauWeb.Dispatch)
description:
## What is wrong

`STA-24` says of abandonment that the restriction ends at "that flow's operation naming the machine: the destroy, or the stop that stands in for it (`ARC-22`), whose own barrier then holds the box plane". `TauWeb.Dispatch.dispatchesContinuation` carries it as `.abandon, k => k == .destroy`, and no theorem reads that case: changed to `.abandon, _ => false`, `lake build` in `tools/formal` still succeeds (rehearsed on a scratch copy at `f801f0a`). Every other clause of the disposition rule has a decided theorem that fails when the clause is removed.

## Why it was left

`ARC-21` runs abandonment "never through a session", the module's `Request` is what a model sends, and the emitter labels every request a model request. A decided, tagged trace in which a destroy is dispatched under an abandonment disposition would put into `docs/design/dispatch-witnesses-v2.json` a model's destroy dispatched as the abandonment, which the Markdown does not say; `docs/design/witness-file-v1.md` states that the file holds no such trace.

## What done looks like

A check fails when the abandonment case of `dispatchesContinuation` is removed or widened, and the witness file still tells a comparing implementation nothing about a model's request for a destroy. Two routes were seen: carry who sends a request and label the abandonment flow's an operator act (ADR-0032's vocabulary has one), which changes the witness file's shape and so its schema version; or decide it by a theorem that is not a witness. The choice needs the maintainer.
close_reason: Implemented TauWeb.Dispatch.abandonment_ends_at_its_destroy_alone, with the controls formal: abandonment never ends at destroy and formal: abandonment also ends at reset. Each mutation fails exactly that theorem, while kinds_total stays green; no abandonment request trace was added.

title: Specify the harness route from LNVPS arch login to root
description:

(`docs/findings/2026-10-11-lnvps-phase-b.md`, observation 3). `OPN-24` tests that the
image accepts the operator's key on its default user. No requirement owns the route
from that login to root.

This blocks the root-only job-record setup in `STA-20` and T42's fixed reads:
`sshd -T` needs the root-only host keys, and the local-account check reads
`/etc/shadow`. The harness-composed delivery reads and the fresh-image checklist run
need a defined execution route too. The owner chose `arch` login and password-free sudo for each job on 2026-11-01.
The specification has not yet incorporated that decision; the executable amendment
brief and remaining verification obligations are recorded in this issue.

Resolve in the specification before the fresh-image checklist is treated as evidence:
name how root is obtained from the default user, what authorizes it, how credentials
are handled if needed, and what refusal means. Keep that route usable when the
checklist requires every password field to be locked or disabled; the selected sudo route
must remain usable after lockdown and reboot. Add conformance coverage for the chosen route and its
failure. Until then no assertion is made about the actual image's sudo policy or
whether it passes the checklist.

comments.text:
## Specification amendment brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Specify the chosen LNVPS route from `arch` to root for every job and protected-record collection, preserving existing tracking and uncertainty rules.

**Current behavior:**
ADR-0051 records that "The route from LNVPS's default login user to root remains a separate open requirement; locking a password used by that route could break it." The recorded fresh-image observation establishes pinned login as `arch`, not password-free sudo or successful lockdown. The specification requires protected job records and root-dependent reads but does not state their access route.

**Desired behavior and settled decision:**
The owner chose A on 2026-11-01: subsequent LNVPS jobs log in as `arch` with the existing per-machine SSH key and switch to root through password-free, non-interactive sudo for each job. Protected-record collection uses the same access route. The route remains usable after password locking, lockdown and reboot, on fresh connections, during later re-entry and for model-free Replace. Decision A excludes direct root login and alternate-login fallback; this exclusion does not come from the credential inventory. No elevation password or interactive prompt is authorized.

A single journaled tracked launcher may acquire root, create the protected job directory and its own record, then start payload work. State its contract without introducing separately dispatched untracked setup. Initial setup, launch and collection must preserve command identity, byte comparison, boot identity, command/runner liveness and file-redirected output. Collection remains the existing permitted read, never arbitrary repair or ordinary `exec` under another label.

Startup and collection failure outcomes are already decided, not a fresh policy frontier. `STA-20` says "A missing record is unresolved, never proof of death." A dispatched sudo or setup attempt lacking its protected record stays unresolved and holds its machine; diagnostics alone do not settle it or authorize retry. Distinguish refusal before transmission, a finished protected record including nonzero exit, and unavailable collection. A reachable machine whose record cannot be read supplies no liveness or completion evidence; show the unavailable collection promptly and preserve uncertainty. Do not wait as though an unreadable record established a live command.

**Requirement owners:**
- The LNVPS-specific login and sudo route belongs to `STG-21`, with references wherever it is used; the generic checklist stays vendor-neutral.
- Generic launcher, directory/record creation and permitted collection belong to `STA-20`. Preserve `STA-20a`'s "Output MUST be captured by redirection to a file, never by reading a pipe the job holds open" and its generic POSIX requirements.
- `ARC-8` owns "Recording commits **per command**, before transmission." `STA-21` owns the sent/received comparison, demonstrated by `CNF-56`: "The command recorded by the machine matches the command the browser journal recorded before sending." Make the launcher/payload representation explicit without weakening that equality.
- `ARC-43` owns read evidence and verdicts: "a read refused or held before dispatch, or with no record, settles nothing". Root-route failure supplies no successful lockdown or delivery evidence.
- `STG-9` requires "at least one later session re-enters over the same pinned channel and re-runs the check". `STA-17` owns Replace's key installation, new-key confirmation, old-key removal and held-machine handling. Apply A to the `arch` account in that flow without changing its ordering or claiming an incomplete migration finished.
- `SEC-11` requires "An SSH session MUST check the host key against the stored fingerprint, and a key that does not match MUST halt the session." Root launch and collection provide no exception.
- `STA-20`'s input rule says "the job wrapper MUST NOT write that input to any file but the job's destination". Preserve placed-secret input through sudo, including relevant capture/logging behavior, and test it against existing secret-handling rules.
- `STG-21` says "Stage 1 still waits for the integrated conformance in `07-conformance.md`; a failure there blocks stage completion." Missing elevation leaves relevant checks/flows incomplete. Do not change `OPN-24`'s vendor target criteria by implication.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] The normative route states A, its authorization and persistence, no password/prompt/alternate-login fallback, and protected collection through the same route. References do not duplicate the rule.
- [ ] Startup creates and uses the protected directory/record within the same tracked launch before ordinary payload work. Launch and collection preserve command comparison, recorded boot identity, detached liveness and file output; no untracked successful setup is introduced.
- [ ] Conformance distinguishes pre-transmission refusal, recorded nonzero exit, sudo/authorization/password/terminal/setup failure after dispatch with no record, disconnect around record creation, and unavailable collection. Missing or unreadable records never release the hold, create successful evidence or cause an automatic retry.
- [ ] Conformance exercises fresh privileged collection while dispatch is held, with no collection deadlock, no arbitrary command admitted as collection, and an immediate visible unavailable-collection result that settles nothing.
- [ ] Conformance exercises the selected route after locked/disabled password fields, lockdown, disconnect, reboot, later fresh-session re-entry and Replace key migration. Changed host keys halt before root work; other machines retain their existing independence.
- [ ] Conformance covers byte equality through the launcher, command/runner liveness through sudo, and placed-secret input without extra capture or consumption by a prompt. Retain relevant existing cases, including `CNF-16`, `CNF-20`, `CNF-40`, `CNF-55`, `CNF-56` and `CNF-108`; any new item acquires its applicable stage row and required tier metadata.
- [ ] Land the normative rule before recording its rationale. Update ADR-0051's now-open-route statement and record the choice and rejected alternatives without writing a second normative copy.
- [ ] Run the repository's required gates before and after the amendment. Leave T42's fresh-image run and integrated evidence explicitly outstanding until demonstrated; a green specification gate is not a live-image result.

**Boundaries and readiness:**
This issue is ready for the bounded specification amendment, not closed and not evidence that the image or integrated harness passes. No new startup exception, terminal evidence, dispatch kind or Lean command-hold change is needed for A. Do not weaken the missing-record rule, hold, theorem, gate or assumption boundary; any later proposal changing those semantics requires separate review. title: Does a reinstall end a placement's required reference?

title: Does an outstanding rescue activation hold the delivery reboot?
description:
`STA-24` says "An unresolved activation or key registration touches no running system and blocks nothing on the box." ADR-0048 follows it for the delivery reboot: "The delivery reboot is box-plane work, held by `STA-20`; it can be issued beside an unresolved activation."

On a vendor with rescue activation, an activation that has not yet been consumed by a reset makes the next boot a rescue boot. A `delivery_reboot` issued then boots the machine into rescue; `ARC-43` settles the call by its boot change, and the delivery check runs against the rescue system, without `STA-20b`'s planned-reset prerequisites or a reset intent. A model `exec` of a reboot has the same exposure.

Decide whether an outstanding rescue activation holds a reboot on the box, or whether the delivery reboot's settlement or the delivery check must refuse a rescue boot. The dedicated path is not offered before stage 3.
